exposure: Specific bacterial pathogens (Escherichia coli, Group B Streptococcus)
cohort: The study included infants born with a gestational age of at least 22 weeks and a birth weight greater than 400g, from 18 centers of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Neonatal Research Network.
finding: Early-onset sepsis incidence and associated mortality disproportionately occurred in preterm infants, with a notable increase in Escherichia coli infections among very low-birth-weight infants compared to previous surveillance periods, underscoring limitations in current Group B Streptococcus prevention strategies.
followup_time: At least 5 days post-birth or until death (for confirmed EOS cases); primary EOS definition within 72 hours of birth.
birth_weight: Greater than 400g (with specific analysis for very low-birth-weight infants 401-1500g).
gest_age: At least 22 weeks (with specific analysis for 22-28 weeks and <37 weeks).
